plain: To scatter and fade away until nothing is left

webster.text: To scatter; to disperse; to drive asunder.

more.text: To expend; to squander; to scatter property in wasteful extravagance; to waste; to consume; as, a man has dissipated his fortune in the pursuit of pleasure.
To scatter; to disperse; to separate into parts and disappear; to waste away; to vanish.

example.quote: Or if the combustible materials that now seem to be collecting should be dissipated without coming to maturity, or if a flame should be kindled without extending to us, what security can we have that our tranquillity will long remain undisturbed from some other cause or from some other quarter?
